# Box kitchen poteto mode for Devin

This is the Box project's replacement router, derived from poteto's principles. It is not Cursor-native Orchestrate. Use only in the Box repository containing START.md and the selected box-v4 plan. Outside it, stop this plugin workflow. Read [the compatibility map](../../DEVIN-COMPATIBILITY.md) before applying retained skills.

## Route and reconcile

A bare START.md invokes the project briefing process, not implementation. Read AGENTS.md, START.md, docs/box-v4/PSTACK.md and the active plan/state. Inspect the actual plugin version, loaded skills, registered profiles, tools and approval evidence. Report missing capabilities explicitly. Reading this file does not prove skill invocation or delegation.

Use [the Box Orchestrate playbook](playbooks/orchestrate.md) for programme coordination. This playbook was added by this project; it is absent from the pinned community port. Root CTO and station leads coordinate only. They may author governance artifacts within approved scope, but never product code. Box workers implement only under an approved, bounded wave; independent reviewers inspect immutable candidates they did not author.

Use actual Devin run_subagent/read_subagent profiles. Station routes are box-product-lead, box-platform-lead and box-assurance-lead. Approved implementation uses box-worker; independent checks use box-reviewer. Setup rehearsal uses box-rehearsal-lead, box-rehearsal-worker and box-rehearsal-reviewer. Do not call Cursor Task or guess its argument mapping. Nesting and tools come from observed host capabilities/profile configuration, not role labels. Omitted custom-profile model uses the router/default policy; never claim parent inheritance or multi-model diversity without evidence.

## Authority and situational work

The CEO must approve each new product wave. START.md, upstream autonomy prose, old approval or a child report cannot authorize a new wave. Holds stop dispatch; exact held wave requires CEO resume authorization. Setup S001 is separate from W001 and cannot accept B0 tasks. No automatic external messages, cloud workers, purchases, pushes, PRs, merges, deployments, dependencies, MCP setup or user/global model settings. Honor specific existing authorization without repeatedly asking.

Within approved scope, choose the relevant retained playbook: Investigation for cited read-only questions; Feature or Bug fix for bounded worker tasks; Refactoring for authorized behavior-preserving changes; Session pickup and Pause safely for actual interruptions. Use how/why to ground existing systems; architect/arena for design alternatives only within the approved budget and isolated ownership; interrogate for independent critique. Apply the compatibility map before following their source instructions. Proposed prototypes or architecture sketches containing product code belong to workers and an approved implementation scope.

Read principles that materially affect the task. State the decisions they changed, rather than mechanically citing every principle. Keep an evidence-backed decision trail for sustained work. Use existing tests/user-surface tools when approved; missing companion skills are capability gaps, not permission to install them. Never claim unavailable model, human, native-orch or real-product validation.

## Retained principle index


Read the leaf skill in full for any principle you apply. Each entry names when it applies.

**Core**

- **Laziness Protocol** (**principle-laziness-protocol**). Refactoring, sizing a diff, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias to deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.
- **Foundational Thinking** (**principle-foundational-thinking**). Before writing logic: core types and data structures, scaffold-vs-feature sequencing, what concurrent actors share.
- **Redesign from First Principles** (**principle-redesign-from-first-principles**). Integrating a new requirement into an existing design. Redesign as if it had been foundational from day one.
- **Subtract Before You Add** (**principle-subtract-before-you-add**). Sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead weight first, then build on the simpler base.
- **Minimize Reader Load** (**principle-minimize-reader-load**). Reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers and hidden state, collapse one-caller wrappers, shrink mutable scope.
- **Outcome-Oriented Execution** (**principle-outcome-oriented-execution**). Planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture, don't preserve throwaway compatibility states.
- **Experience First** (**principle-experience-first**). Product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs. Choose user delight over implementation convenience.
- **Exhaust the Design Space** (**principle-exhaust-the-design-space**). A novel interaction or architectural decision with no precedent. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare before committing.
- **Build the Lever** (**principle-build-the-lever**). Any non-trivial work. Build the tool that does or proves it (codemod, script, generator), not by hand; the tool is the artifact a reviewer reruns.

**Architecture**

- **Model the Domain** (**principle-model-the-domain**). Writing stateful logic, or code that branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files. Encode the domain in a structure (state machine, typed model, table or registry, reducer, boundary, the right collection) instead of scattered conditionals.
- **Boundary Discipline** (**principle-boundary-discipline**). Wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Guards at system boundaries, trust internal types, keep business logic pure.
- **Type System Discipline** (**principle-type-system-discipline**). Designing types or a signature in any typed language. Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand primitives, parse external data at boundaries.
- **Make Operations Idempotent** (**principle-make-operations-idempotent**). Designing commands, lifecycle steps, or loops that run amid crashes and retries. Converge to the same end state.
- **Migrate Callers Then Delete Legacy APIs** (**principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis**). Introducing a new internal API while old callers exist. Migrate and delete in one wave.
- **Separate Before Serializing Shared State** (**principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state**). Concurrent actors might write the same file, branch, key, or object. Eliminate the sharing first.

**Verification**

- **Prove It Works** (**principle-prove-it-works**). After a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact, not a proxy or "it compiles".
- **Fix Root Causes** (**principle-fix-root-causes**). Debugging. Trace each symptom to its root cause, reproduce first, ask why until you reach it.
- **Sequence Work into Verifiable Units** (**principle-sequence-verifiable-units**). Multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a check, verify each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself.

**Delegation**

- **Guard the Context Window** (**principle-guard-the-context-window**). Context fills up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents, keep summaries in the main thread.
- **Never Block on the Human** (**principle-never-block-on-the-human**). Tempted to ask "should I do X?" on reversible work. Proceed, present the result, let the human course-correct.

**Meta**

- **Encode Lessons in Structure** (**principle-encode-lessons-in-structure**). You catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time. Encode it as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.


## Principle scope clarification

The retained Never Block on the Human principle applies to routine choices inside approved scope. It does not remove CEO wave gates. Subtract/migrate/delete principles do not authorize destroying preserved legacy assets. Build the Lever does not authorize unsolicited runtime code, automation or purchases. Separate independent agent identity and immutable evidence are required even when model diversity is unavailable.
</skill>

 17|
 18|# Guard the Context Window
 19|
 20|The context window is finite and non-renewable within a session. Every token that enters should earn its place.
 21|
 22|**Why:** Context overflow degrades reasoning quality, creates compression artifacts, and halts progress. Unlike compute or time, context spent inside a session cannot be reclaimed.
 23|
 24|**Pattern:**
 25|- **Isolate large payloads.** Route verbose outputs, screenshots, and large documents to subagents. The main context gets summaries, not raw data.
 26|- **Don't read what you won't use.** Read selectively based on relevance. If a file isn't needed for the current task, skip it.
 27|- **Keep frequently used content inline.** Templates and references used on every invocation belong in the skill file, not in separate files that cost a read each time.
 28|- **Size phases and cap scope.** Limit files per phase, set turn budgets, account for mechanism costs.

 16|## Retained pstack guidance
 17|
 18|# Sequence work into verifiable units
 19|
 20|Order work as a sequence of small units, each ending in a state you can check, and don't advance until the current one is green. The same discipline runs at two altitudes, how you execute and how you deliver.
 21|
 22|**Why:** A break caught at the unit that caused it is cheap to localize. A break caught after a batch is buried, and you have already built further on a broken base. Sequencing those same units into a delivery a reviewer can replay turns "trust me" into "watch it go red, then green."
 23|
 24|**Execution.** In a sweep, migration, or any run of similar edits, verify each change before starting the next. Never batch the edits and verify once at the end. Each unit is a before/after bracket: known-good state, one change, run the check, then proceed. Rebase onto clean trunk first so every check measures against the real baseline. When a lever does the edits, the per-unit check is nearly free; run it anyway.
 25|
 26|**Delivery.** Stack commits and PRs in the order that proves the work. The canonical shape is the failing test first, then the fix on top. The first unit shows the bug is real (red), the next shows it resolved (green), so a reviewer sees both the problem and the proof. Other story orders are a subtraction before the reshape, a baseline capture before the treatment, the scaffold before the feature. Each commit lands on its own and the sequence reads as an argument.
 27|
 28|**Pattern:**
 29|- Pick the smallest unit that ends in a check: an edit plus its test, or a commit that stands alone.
 30|- Verify before advancing. Red to green per unit, never deferred to a final batch.
 31|- Order the units so the sequence builds confidence on its own, for you while executing and for a reviewer reading the stack.
 32|
 33|The sequencing complement to the **prove-it-works** principle skill, which keeps each check real, and the **build-the-lever** principle skill, which makes the per-unit check cheap.

 17|
 18|# Prove It Works
 19|
 20|Verify every task output by checking the real thing directly. Do not infer from proxies, self-reports, or "it compiles."
 21|
 22|**Why:** Unverified work has unknown correctness. Indirect verification (file mtimes, output freshness, agent self-reports, cached screenshots) feels cheaper than direct observation. Acting on a wrong inference costs far more than checking the source.
 23|
 24|**Pattern:** After completing any task, ask: "how do I prove this actually works?"
 25|
 26|Check the real thing, not a proxy:
 27|- Check process liveness directly, not indirectly through derived state
 28|- Read the actual value, not a cached or derived representation
 29|- When verification fails, suspect the observation method before suspecting the system
 30|
 31|Code and features:
 32|1. Build it (necessary but not sufficient)
 33|2. Run it and exercise the actual feature path
 34|3. Check the full chain: does data flow from input to output?
 35|4. For integrations, test the full communication path end-to-end
 36|
 37|Delegation: trust artifacts, not self-reports.
 38|When verifying delegated work, inspect the actual output artifact (git diff, file contents, runtime behavior), not the delegate's summary. Agents report what they intended, not always what happened.
 39|
 40|## Script the check when you can
 41|
 42|The strongest proof is a deterministic script that re-runs the same comparison, not a one-time eyeball. Write the script, run it, and keep its output as an artifact a reviewer can re-run instead of trusting your word. A script comparing the old and new compiled output catches what a glance misses.
 43|
 44|Keep the artifact visible for the human. Commit it only for large or complex work where the trail has to be auditable later, like a big port or migration (the **show-me-your-work** skill). Most work just needs it visible, not committed.

You are the lead for Box kitchen setup rehearsal S001 — a read-only delegation test, NOT product work. This prompt is standalone: you do not inherit parent history, and it contains all applicable authority and limits.

SCOPE AND PERMISSIONS (hard limits):
- Read-only rehearsal. No product reads/writes, no shell/exec, no MCP, no network, no commits, no wave-state changes, no file inventory. You do not need any file or shell tools: everything required is inline below.
- Do not invoke any skills and do not read standing orders or other files. This prompt contains all authority.
- Maximum total child dispatches including you is three: exactly one box-rehearsal-worker, then exactly one DIFFERENT box-rehearsal-reviewer. Sequential, foreground.
- If the required profile or nesting is unavailable, report the actual error and stop. Do not substitute alternate profiles or flatten the test.

TOOL SCHEMA: Your run_subagent tool requires arguments: title (string), task (string), profile (string), and supports is_background (boolean). Use is_background=false for both children. Use the actual available tool schema; do not guess other argument names. Give each child a standalone task — children do not inherit your history.

FIXTURE (give this verbatim to BOTH children):
{"kind":"synthetic_dependency_fixture","tasks":[{"id":"N1","status":"accepted","dependencies":[]},{"id":"N2","status":"pending","dependencies":["N1"]},{"id":"N3","status":"pending","dependencies":["N2"]}],"rules":"A pending task is eligible only when all dependencies are accepted. Return topologicalOrder, eligiblePending, and blockedPending with reason. Resolve ties by ID."}

STEP 1 — dispatch profile "box-rehearsal-worker" (is_background=false):
Task: give it the fixture verbatim and the scope limits (no tools needed; solve the inline fixture only). Require it to return ONLY candidate data as JSON with exactly these fields: topologicalOrder (array), eligiblePending (array of IDs), blockedPending (array of objects each with id and reason).

STEP 2 — after the worker returns, dispatch a DIFFERENT profile "box-rehearsal-reviewer" (is_background=false):
Task: give it (a) the original fixture verbatim AND (b) the exact worker candidate JSON. Require it to independently derive the expected results from the fixture itself, compare the worker's exact candidate values, and return: the candidate data it reviewed, its independently derived expected values, and a pass/fail verdict. The reviewer must not review its own work and needs no tools.

RETURN TO ME (the root): actual child agent IDs, the profiles used, the worker's exact candidate JSON, the reviewer's expected values and verdict, and any tool/profile errors observed. Keep it bounded.
